Per : Justice Alok Awasthi Heard on IA No.16711/2025, which is an application filed by the appellant under Section 7A of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2006 (in short "the JJ Act") seeking a fresh determination of his juvenility on the date of commission of the offence i.e. 14.10.2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2006
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Appellant stands convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 323/34, 342, 376(D),
376(2)(N) and 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 06 months with fine of Rs.500/-, RI for 06 months with fine of Rs.500/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/-, RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- and RI for 03 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively with default stipulations vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.09.2017 passed by the 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, District Dhar in S.T. No.191/2016.
3.
As per prosecution story, on 14.10.2015, the appellant alongwith co-accused persons committed rape upon the prosecutrix repeatedly.

FIR was 2 CRA-5254-2017 lodged on 16.10.2015.
4.
During pendency of the appeal, the appellant preferred an application before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Dhar claiming juvenility.
Learned CJM conducted a detailed enquiry under Section 7A of the JJ Act.

The appellant has not produced his Aadhaar Card himself, but the same has been produced by the complainant alongwith the statement of his mother and the report of the ossification test conducted by the doctor.
The ossification test indicated the appellant's age between 16 to 18 years.

However, learned CJM, placing reliance upon the Aadhaar Card which clearly showed the appellant to be a major on the date of the incident, held that the appellant was not a juvenile on 14.10.2015 and rejected the application.
The said order of learned CJM was never challenged by the appellant and has attained finality.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Trial Court erred in not treating the appellant as a juvenile because the prosecutrix in her statement had estimated the appellant's age as 16-17 years.
He prays for a fresh determination of age and for forwarding the appellant to the Juvenile Justice Board.

6. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the application submitting that the claim of juvenility has already been adjudicated by a Competent Court (CJM) on the basis of documentary evidence (Aadhaar Card) and the said finding has attained finality.
The prosecutrix's estimate of age is not admissible or reliable evidence for determination of juvenility.
The application is therefore liable to be rejected.
3 CRA-5254-2017 7. Learned counsel for the objector has also prayed for rejection of the application.

8. Section 7A of the JJ Act mandates that whenever a claim of juvenility is raised before any Court or at any stage, the Court shall make an inquiry and take such evidence as may be necessary to determine the age of the person.
However, the statute does not contemplate repeated or successive inquiries once the claim has already been adjudicated by a competent Court after due inquiry and the order has attained finality.

9. In the present case, learned CJM, after conducting a proper inquiry and considering the Aadhaar Card, statement of the mother and the ossification report, categorically held the appellant to be a major on the date of the offence.
The Aadhaar Card is a statutory document issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India and carries a presumption of correctness unless proved otherwise.
No material has been placed before this Court to doubt the authenticity or correctness of the date of birth mentioned in the Aadhaar Card.
The order of learned CJM was not assailed by the appellant and has therefore attained finality.

The appellant cannot be permitted to reagitate the same issue before this Court in the absence of any fresh, unimpeachable and clinching evidence showing that he was below 18 years of age on 14.10.2015.
10.
The only ground now pressed by the appellant is the prosecutrix's statement estimating the appellant's age as 16-17 years.
This Court finds the submission wholly untenable.
The age of the accused cannot be determined on the basis of a victim's visual estimate or rough assessment made during 4 CRA-5254-2017 the incident.
Such estimation is neither scientific nor documentary evidence and cannot override the documentary proof (Aadhaar Card) relied upon by learned CJM.

The ossification test report itself shows the age as 16-18 years -- a range that includes both juvenile and non-juvenile status -- and therefore cannot be read in favour of the appellant when a more reliable document (Aadhaar Card) is available.

11. It is also pertinent to note that the offence in question is dated 14.10.2015, the law as applicable at the relevant time and the subsequent statutory scheme do not warrant interference at this stage,
particularly when the claim has already been rejected after due inquiry and not challenged.

sentences.text: In view of the above, this Court finds no merit in the present application.
The claim of juvenility is declined.
Accordingly, IA No.16711/2025 stands rejected.
